evals.query: I have a Kora 2.0 HTTP server in Java. Expose my OpenAPI spec at /api/openapi and an interactive Swagger UI at /api/docs.
expected_behavior: Adds implementation "io.koraframework:openapi-management" and keeps io.koraframework:http-server-undertow, with versions coming from the io.koraframework:kora-bom platform (koraVersion=2.0.0.RC2) rather than pinned per artifact
Adds OpenApiManagementModule (io.koraframework.openapi.management.OpenApiManagementModule) to the @KoraApp extends list alongside UndertowPublicHttpServerModule
Places the spec under src/main/resources/openapi/ and lists it in openapi.management.files (plural)
Sets openapi.management.enabled = true, path = "/api/openapi", swaggerui.enabled = true and swaggerui.path = "/api/docs"
Uses the key names path / swaggerui.path, never the Kora 1.x endpoint / swaggerui.endpoint
Notes that enabled and swaggerui.enabled both default to false, and that enabled = true is required for the UI to have anything to fetch
Does not use ru.tinkoff.kora coordinates or packages, and does not pull in an external documentation library

evals.query: Kotlin Kora 2.0 service. Publish openapi/api.yaml and turn on the Scalar viewer.
expected_behavior: Uses ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors") plus implementation("io.koraframework:openapi-management") and implementation("io.koraframework:http-server-undertow")
Declares interface Application : HoconConfigModule, UndertowPublicHttpServerModule, OpenApiManagementModule with a top-level fun main() calling KoraApplication.run(ApplicationGraph::graph)
Sets openapi.management.enabled = true, files = ["openapi/api.yaml"] and scalar.enabled = true
States the resulting routes GET /openapi and GET /scalar
Does not use suspend functions, Context, or any ru.tinkoff.kora package

evals.query: I am porting a Kora 1.x service to 2.0. My application.conf has openapi.management.file = ["openapi/api.yaml"] and openapi.management.endpoint = "/openapi", and now the app dies on startup with ConfigValueException: Config expected value, but got null after parsing at path: 'ROOT.openapi.management.files'. What happened?
expected_behavior: Identifies that the 2.0 key is files (plural) and that file is not read at all — an unknown HOCON key is ignored without a warning
Explains that files has no default and is not nullable, so the whole openapi.management object fails to map while the DI graph is being built
States that this happens even when enabled = false, because the config component is created eagerly for the module's request handlers
Also renames endpoint to path, and notes that this second rename fails silently — the specs would appear on the default /openapi
Gives the corrected block: openapi.management { enabled = true; files = ["openapi/api.yaml"]; path = "/openapi" }
Does not claim that the endpoint serves an empty document; the failure is a startup ConfigValueException

evals.query: Our Kora config still has openapi.management.rapidoc.enabled = true but /rapidoc returns 404 after the 2.0 upgrade. How do I get RapiDoc back?
expected_behavior: States that RapiDoc does not exist in Kora 2.0 — io.koraframework.openapi.management ships only OpenApiHttpServerHandler, SwaggerUIHttpServerHandler, SwaggerOauthHttpServerHandler and ScalarHttpServerHandler, and OpenApiManagementConfig has no rapidoc accessor
Explains that the rapidoc block is an unknown HOCON key: ignored silently, no viewer served, hence the 404
Replaces it with scalar { enabled = true } and states the default route GET /scalar (configurable via scalar.path)
Notes that anything pointing at /rapidoc — ingress rules, bookmarks, smoke tests — must be updated
Does not suggest adding an external RapiDoc dependency or hand-writing a controller to host RapiDoc

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 app starts fine and /swagger-ui renders, but the spec request comes back 404 with "OpenAPI file not found while reading: src/main/resources/openapi/api.yaml". Why?
expected_behavior: Explains that files entries are classpath resource paths, not filesystem paths — the value must be openapi/api.yaml, not src/main/resources/openapi/api.yaml
Notes the resource is resolved with getResourceAsStream(path) and then getResourceAsStream("/" + path), so a leading slash is fine but a source-tree prefix is not
Explains why startup stayed green: the resource is read lazily on the first request, so a wrong path surfaces as a 404 from the endpoint rather than a graph build failure
Suggests confirming the file lands in build/resources/main/

Mentions that under nativeCompile the application's own spec must also be registered in its own META-INF/native-image/<group>/resource-config.json, since openapi-management registers only its bundled viewer pages

evals.query: I added io.koraframework:openapi-management and extended OpenApiManagementModule in my @KoraApp, but no /openapi or /swagger-ui route exists and no HTTP port is listening. My app only extends HoconConfigModule, LogbackModule and OpenApiManagementModule.
expected_behavior: Identifies that OpenApiManagementModule only contributes HttpServerRequestHandler components and starts no server
Adds implementation "io.koraframework:http-server-undertow" and makes @KoraApp extend UndertowPublicHttpServerModule
Uses UndertowPublicHttpServerModule, not the Kora 1.x UndertowHttpServerModule, which no longer exists
Notes that the docs handlers are untagged, so they are served by the public server on httpServer.port and never appear on httpServer.system.port
Does not suggest writing an @HttpController to serve the spec by hand

evals.query: I wrote an HttpServerInterceptor annotated @Component and @Tag(HttpServerModule.class) to require an Authorization header on /swagger-ui. It compiles, the app starts, but the docs are still reachable without a header. Java, Kora 2.0.
expected_behavior: Identifies the tag as the bug: the global interceptor tag in Kora 2.0 is @Tag(HttpServer.class) from io.koraframework.http.server.common.HttpServer

Explains that HttpServerModule still exists as a type, so @Tag(HttpServerModule.class) compiles, but publicHttpApiRouter claims interceptors only by @Tag(HttpServer.class) — nothing collects the component and it silently never runs
Shows the synchronous 2.0 contract: HttpServerResponse intercept(HttpServerRequest request, InterceptChain chain), with no Context parameter and no CompletionStage
Returns HttpServerResponse.of(401, HttpBody.plaintext(...)) for unauthorized docs requests and calls chain.process(request) for everything else
Reads the header with request.headers().getFirst("Authorization") and the path with request.path()
Recommends covering it with a test that asserts an unauthenticated GET /swagger-ui is rejected, because the failure mode is silent

evals.query: Kotlin Kora 2.0: keep Swagger UI and Scalar enabled in production but require a bearer token to reach /openapi, /swagger-ui and /scalar.
expected_behavior: Implements class ...(: HttpServerInterceptor) with override fun intercept(request: HttpServerRequest, chain: HttpServerInterceptor.InterceptChain): HttpServerResponse
Annotates it @Component and @Tag(HttpServer::class), importing io.koraframework.http.server.common.HttpServer
Checks request.path() against the /openapi, /swagger-ui and /scalar prefixes and calls chain.process(request) for every other request
Returns HttpServerResponse.of(401, HttpBody.plaintext("Unauthorized")) when the token is missing or wrong
Does not use suspend, CompletionStage, Context, or a servlet-style filter
Mentions the alternative of turning swaggerui.enabled / scalar.enabled off per environment

evals.query: Publish both api-v1.yaml and api-v2.yaml so Swagger UI lets me switch between the two versions.
expected_behavior: Lists both files in openapi.management.files = ["openapi/api-v1.yaml", "openapi/api-v2.yaml"]
Explains that with two or more entries the raw-spec route becomes {path}/{file}, so the documents are at /openapi/api-v1 and /openapi/api-v2 — there is no combined document at /openapi
States that {file} is the basename with directory and .json/.yml/.yaml extension stripped
Warns that basenames must be unique, because the handler indexes specs by stripped basename and duplicates collapse onto one route
Enables openapi.management.enabled and swaggerui.enabled so the UI renders a selector

evals.query: I set openapi.management.swaggerui.options { filter = "false" } in my Kora 2.0 config and now Swagger UI lost deep linking, the operation ids and the standalone layout. Why?
expected_behavior: Explains that options is a Map<String,String> with a default of seven entries, and that the default is used only when the key is absent — supplying options replaces the whole map rather than merging into it
Tells the user to repeat every entry they want to keep: layout, validatorUrl, defaultModelsExpandDepth, deepLinking, persistAuthorization, displayOperationId, filter
Notes that values are HOCON strings which are emitted as raw JS literals when they look like null/true/false, a number, an object, an array or a function, and as quoted strings otherwise
Does not invent typed sub-keys such as swaggerui.deepLinking or swaggerui.layout

evals.query: Keep the raw OpenAPI document reachable for tooling but hide the interactive viewers in production.
expected_behavior: Keeps openapi.management.enabled = true so the raw-spec route stays registered
Sets openapi.management.swaggerui.enabled = false and openapi.management.scalar.enabled = false in the production override
Optionally drives the toggles from the environment with a HOCON optional substitution such as enabled = ${?SWAGGER_UI_ENABLED}
Explains that a disabled handler is skipped by the router, so its route is not registered and requests fall through to a normal 404
Does not rely on a profile annotation; the toggles are pure config under openapi.management

evals.query: I generate my Kora 2.0 server from http-server.yaml with the kora generator. How do I also publish that exact document plus Swagger UI?
expected_behavior: Adds io.koraframework:openapi-management next to the existing org.openapi.generator codegen and OpenApiManagementModule on the @KoraApp graph
Points openapi.management.files at the same src/main/resources/openapi/http-server.yaml that the GenerateTask uses as inputSpec
Explains that the file is already on the classpath under src/main/resources, so no copy task is needed and the published document cannot drift from the generated transport layer
Sets openapi.management.enabled = true and swaggerui.enabled = true, giving GET /openapi and GET /swagger-ui
Notes that files accepts either a HOCON list or a single comma-separated string
Does not hand-write a controller to serve the document

evals.query: Kora 2.0: /swagger-ui renders but shows "Failed to load API definition". My config is openapi.management { files = ["openapi/api.yaml"], swaggerui { enabled = true } }.
expected_behavior: Identifies the missing openapi.management.enabled = true — it defaults to false, so the raw-spec route the UI fetches is never registered
Explains that swaggerui.enabled only registers the UI page; the page derives the document URL from the current URL by replacing swaggerui.path with path
Gives the fixed config with enabled = true
Does not blame the spec content or suggest an external viewer
